answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with decaying reputation quotas. Like a trellis that only supports vines that keep growing, each identity starts with a tiny transaction quota that rises slowly through successful, verified exchanges and falls on inactivity or fraud. Crossing the ridge from newcomer to trusted trader therefore takes sustained honest time, not just new accounts. An attacker planting a whole orchard of fake identities gains only many tiny quotas, each too small to sway prices or votes, while honest agents keep compounding useful history.
